source_citation: Bob Harms, University of Texas Plant Resources Center, NW Hays County native Mimosa field comparison (online)

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Woody shrub in NW Hays County
morphology_source_reported.stems: Darker with brownish-red new growth, zigzag as contrasted with straight grayish M. borealis
morphology_source_reported.prickles: Narrow, downward-recurved and commonly aligned directly beneath petioles at leaf nodes; M. borealis prickles scattered more randomly
morphology_source_reported.leaves: (1–)1–5(–6) pinna pairs, 3–9(–10) leaflet pairs; counts overlap with M. borealis and not reliable for separation
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Globose pale-pink flower heads; petals fused, in contrast to separate petals in M. borealis; flower color unreliable
morphology_source_reported.phenology: Local observations report later bloom than M. borealis and some flowering after summer rain
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Compared with M. borealis; source notes stalked larger pods of M. borealis but does not provide numerical M. texana pod dimensions

habitat_source_reported: Observed growing naturally in NW Hays County, Texas
cautions: Independent Hays County field observation is not BONAP county-level confirmation
Leaflet counts and flower color overlap species and cannot alone be diagnostic
Source photographs do not have publication rights verified and must not be copied to website yet
Maintain distinctions from other Mimosa biuncifera historical concepts
